The rack module has at least one site for receiving a device for administering a medical product, the site comprising at least one plug for supplying electrical current to the administering device and for data transfer. In order to improve the connection between the rack modules and make their use easier, the invention proposes that the inlet connector or the outlet connector be movable between a storage position and a connected position. The movable connector is referred to as the mobile connector, and the other connector is referred to as the second connector. When a second module is placed above or below the module, the mobile connector, in the connected position, is connected to the second connector of the second module placed above or below the module. This enables one of the connectors to be stored in a safe position, so that during storage and handling of the module there is no risk of the connector being damaged.

The invention relates to a rack module intended to build a support column, for example a rack, by stacking two or more such modules. Each rack module includes at least one location designed to receive a device for delivering a medical product. This location has at least one socket that supplies electrical power to the delivery device and enables data communication.

The module is also equipped with an input connector and an output connector so that two consecutive modules can be connected together. Electrical supply lines and data transmission lines link the input connector both to the socket or sockets of the receiving locations and to the output connector.

To make the connection between rack modules easier and more reliable, the invention proposes that either the input connector or the output connector can move between a storage position and a connection position. The connector capable of moving is referred to as the mobile connector, while the other connector is referred to as the second connector. When another module is positioned above or below the module, the mobile connector, once in its connection position, engages with the second connector of that other module.

This arrangement makes it possible to keep one of the connectors in a protected storage position, reducing the risk of damage during storage and handling of the module.

The invention relates to a rack module designed to form part of a support column for medical equipment. The support column is obtained by stacking at least two rack modules on top of one another, thereby creating a modular structure that can be adapted according to the number of medical devices to be supported and connected.

Each rack module comprises at least one receiving site intended to accommodate a medical product administering device, such as an infusion pump or similar apparatus. This receiving site is equipped with a plug configured to provide both electrical power and data communication to the medical device. As a result, when the device is installed in the rack module, it can be powered and connected for data exchange without requiring separate external cables.

The rack module further includes an inlet connector and an outlet connector. These connectors are electrically and communicatively linked to one another by internal power supply and data transfer lines. This arrangement allows several rack modules to be connected in succession when they are stacked, so that power and data can be transmitted from one module to the next throughout the support column.

At least one of the connectors is movable between a storage position and a connected position. In the storage position, the connector is housed or protected within the rack module, making the module easier and safer to handle before assembly. In the connected position, the connector is displaced so that it can engage with a corresponding connector of an adjacent rack module. This movable configuration simplifies the process of connecting successive modules and helps ensure reliable alignment and connection between them.

By allowing the movable connector to be stored safely during transport, handling, or installation, the rack module reduces the risk of connector damage. This improves the durability of the module and facilitates assembly of a robust, modular support column capable of supplying power and data communication to multiple medical product administering devices.
outputs.L4:
A rack module designed for stacking in a medical support column is provided for receiving and supplying medical administration devices, such as infusion pumps or similar equipment. The rack module includes one or more equipment sites or mounting positions, each configured to hold an administration device and to provide the device with the necessary electrical power and data communication connections. These connections may include power plugs, data plugs, or combined power/data interfaces arranged so that a device mounted at a site can be connected quickly and reliably.

To allow several rack modules to be stacked one above another in a support column, the module is equipped with internal power and data lines that can be electrically connected to corresponding lines in an adjacent module. For this purpose, the rack module includes at least one movable inlet connector or outlet connector. The movable connector is arranged so that, when two rack modules are placed together, it can be shifted into a connection position in which it engages with a mating connector of the neighboring module. In this way, power and data signals can be passed from one module to the next without requiring separate loose cables between the modules.

The movable connector may be mounted so that it can slide, pivot, or otherwise move between at least two positions. In a protected or storage position, the connector is retracted or held within the contour of the rack module, reducing the likelihood that it will be bent, broken, contaminated, or otherwise damaged during transport, storage, cleaning, or installation. When the rack module is to be assembled into the support column, the connector is moved into an operating or connected position, where it projects or aligns sufficiently to engage with the mating connector of the adjacent module.

This arrangement simplifies assembly of the medical support column because the electrical and data connections between successive rack modules can be made as part of the stacking process or immediately after the modules are positioned. It also improves reliability and safety by protecting the connector when it is not in use and by reducing the need for manual cable routing. As a result, the rack modules can be handled more easily, connected more securely, and maintained with a lower risk of damage to the inter-module power and data interfaces.

**The Power of “The” and “This”**

The words **“the”** and **“this”** may seem simple, but they are very important in English. **The** is used to talk about something specific or already known. For example, when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book, not just any book.

**This** is also used to point to something specific, usually something close to the speaker. For example, “this idea” means the idea we are talking about right now.

These small words help make language clear. Without them, sentences can sound confusing or incomplete. **The** gives focus, and **this** creates connection. Together, they help us explain what we mean in a simple and direct way.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a European patent application description of a rack module used to build a support column for medical administering devices, including power and data lines, inlet and outlet connectors, and a mobile connector that connects to another stacked module.
counterfactuals.output:
## Description

### Title

**Rack module for constructing a support column for medical administering devices**

### Technical Field

The invention relates to a rack module for constructing a support column for medical administering devices, in particular for infusion pumps, syringe pumps, nutrition pumps, monitoring units or similar medical devices. The invention further relates to a support column composed of a plurality of such rack modules, wherein electrical power and data signals are conducted through the support column.

### Background Art

In hospitals and other medical environments, it is often necessary to arrange a plurality of medical administering devices in the vicinity of a patient. Such devices may include infusion pumps, syringe pumps, enteral feeding pumps or monitoring and control units. These devices are typically mounted on stands, rails, columns or rack systems.

Known rack systems often comprise a vertical support column on which individual medical devices are mechanically secured. In many cases, each device must be separately connected to a power supply and, where applicable, to a data network. This results in a large number of cables, which may obstruct access to the patient, complicate cleaning and increase the risk of accidental disconnection.

There are also known modular systems in which several pump modules can be stacked or arranged one above another. However, such systems may require complex cabling between modules, or they may have fixed electrical interfaces that are difficult to align during assembly. In addition, known systems may not provide sufficient flexibility for building support columns of different heights or for retrofitting additional modules.

It is therefore desirable to provide a rack module which can be combined with further rack modules in a simple and reliable manner, and which provides both mechanical support and electrical interconnection for medical administering devices.

### Summary of the Invention

The object of the invention is to provide a rack module which permits simple construction of a support column for medical administering devices and which enables reliable transfer of electrical power and data between stacked modules.

This object is achieved by a rack module comprising a module body configured to form a portion of a support column, at least one receiving or mounting region for a medical administering device, at least one power line and at least one data line extending through the module body, an inlet connector and an outlet connector connected to the power and data lines, and a mobile connector arranged movably relative to the module body for connection to a corresponding connector of another rack module stacked with the rack module.

The mobile connector allows compensation of tolerances during assembly of adjacent rack modules. In particular, the mobile connector may be displaceable, pivotable and/or resiliently biased so that it can self-align with a corresponding connector of a neighbouring module. In this way, a reliable electrical connection can be established between stacked rack modules without requiring precise manual positioning of rigid connectors.

The rack module may be configured such that, when a plurality of rack modules are stacked one above another, the power lines and data lines form continuous power and data buses extending through the resulting support column. The inlet connector may receive power and/or data from a lower module, a base unit, a power supply unit or a hospital infrastructure connection. The outlet connector may supply power and/or data to an upper module or to an additional rack module. The mobile connector may be associated with the inlet connector or the outlet connector, or may form one of these connectors.

The rack module may further comprise an internal distribution interface for supplying power and/or data to a medical administering device mounted to the rack module. The medical administering device may be connectable by a device connector provided at the mounting region, so that the device can be powered and optionally controlled or monitored via the rack module.

The modular construction allows a support column to be assembled from a desired number of rack modules. Each rack module can provide a mechanical support position for one or more medical administering devices and can simultaneously contribute to the internal power and data infrastructure of the column.

### Brief Description of the Drawings

Embodiments of the invention are described below with reference to the drawings, in which:

**Fig. 1** shows a perspective view of a support column comprising a plurality of stacked rack modules;

**Fig. 2** shows a schematic sectional view of a rack module with internal power and data lines;

**Fig. 3** shows a detailed view of a mobile connector of the rack module;

**Fig. 4** shows two rack modules during a stacking operation; and

**Fig. 5** shows an embodiment of an electrical connection arrangement comprising an inlet connector, an outlet connector and a device connector.

### Detailed Description of Embodiments

Fig. 1 schematically shows a support column 1 for medical administering devices 2. The support column 1 comprises a plurality of rack modules 3 stacked one above another along a vertical stacking direction V. Each rack module 3 forms a segment of the support column 1 and is mechanically connectable to at least one further rack module 3.

The support column 1 may be mounted on a mobile base 4 having wheels 5, or may be fixed to a wall, ceiling arm, bed rail, trolley or other support structure. The support column 1 may be used in intensive care units, operating theatres, emergency wards or general hospital wards.

Each rack module 3 comprises a module body 6. The module body 6 may be formed as a housing, frame, profile element or structural casing. The module body 6 preferably has an upper connection side 7 and a lower connection side 8. The upper connection side 7 is configured for connection to a lower connection side 8 of another rack module 3, and the lower connection side 8 is configured for connection to an upper connection side 7 of another rack module 3 or to a base unit.

The module body 6 may be made of metal, plastics material or a combination thereof. In a medical environment, the outer surfaces of the module body 6 are preferably smooth and easy to clean. The module body 6 may have rounded edges and sealed joints in order to reduce contamination and facilitate disinfection.

At least one mounting region 9 is provided on the module body 6. The mounting region 9 is configured to receive or support a medical administering device 2. The mounting region 9 may comprise a rail, guide, latch, locking recess, hook, clamp, dovetail profile or other mechanical coupling structure. The medical administering device 2 may be attachable to the rack module 3 by sliding, snapping, pivoting or clamping.

In the embodiment shown, each rack module 3 is adapted to receive one medical administering device 2. In other embodiments, one rack module 3 may receive two or more devices, or may serve only as an intermediate or spacer module without receiving a device.

As shown schematically in Fig. 2, the rack module 3 comprises electrical lines extending through the module body 6. The electrical lines include at least one power line 10 and at least one data line 11. The power line 10 may comprise two or more conductors, for example conductors for direct-current supply voltage and ground. Alternatively or additionally, the power line 10 may comprise conductors for alternating-current mains voltage. The data line 11 may comprise one or more conductors or communication channels, for example for serial communication, Ethernet communication, CAN bus communication, RS-485 communication, USB communication or another wired communication protocol.

The power line 10 and the data line 11 extend between an inlet connector 12 and an outlet connector 13. The inlet connector 12 is configured to receive power and data from an adjacent module, a base unit or an external supply. The outlet connector 13 is configured to pass power and data to another adjacent module. In the assembled support column 1, the inlet and outlet connectors 12, 13 of adjacent rack modules 3 are electrically connected so that the power and data lines 10, 11 of the rack modules 3 together form a continuous column bus.

The inlet connector 12 may be arranged at the lower connection side 8 and the outlet connector 13 may be arranged at the upper connection side 7. Conversely, the inlet connector 12 may be arranged at the upper connection side 7 and the outlet connector 13 at the lower connection side 8, depending on the intended direction of power and data distribution. The terms “inlet” and “outlet” do not necessarily imply a limitation to a particular physical orientation but indicate the functional direction of supply in a typical configuration.

The rack module 3 further comprises a mobile connector 14. The mobile connector 14 is movable relative to the module body 6. In the embodiment illustrated in Fig. 3, the mobile connector 14 is part of the outlet connector 13. In other embodiments, the mobile connector 14 may be part of the inlet connector 12 or may be arranged between the inlet connector 12 and outlet connector 13 as a separate coupling element.

The mobile connector 14 is configured to connect to a corresponding connector 15 of another stacked rack module 3. The corresponding connector 15 may be a fixed connector or may itself be a mobile connector. The mobile connector 14 may comprise electrical contact elements 16 for power transmission and electrical contact elements 17 for data transmission. The contact elements 16, 17 may be formed as pins, sockets, spring contacts, blade contacts, contact pads, pogo pins or other suitable electrical contacts.

The mobile connector 14 is mounted in a connector carrier 18. The connector carrier 18 is received in a guide 19 of the module body 6. The guide 19 permits movement of the connector carrier 18 transverse to the stacking direction V, parallel to the stacking direction V and/or angularly relative to the module body 6. In this way, the mobile connector 14 can compensate for manufacturing tolerances, assembly tolerances or slight misalignment between adjacent rack modules 3.

In one embodiment, the mobile connector 14 is floatingly mounted. For example, the connector carrier 18 may be held in the module body 6 with play in at least one lateral direction. A resilient element 20, such as a spring, elastomer body or resilient plastics web, may bias the mobile connector 14 toward a neutral position. During stacking, the corresponding connector 15 of the adjacent rack module 3 engages the mobile connector 14 and displaces it from the neutral position if necessary until the electrical contacts are aligned.

In another embodiment, the mobile connector 14 is linearly displaceable along the stacking direction V. This permits the connector to retract slightly during assembly and to be pressed into an operative contact position by a spring force. Such an arrangement may reduce mechanical stress on the connector contacts.

In a further embodiment, the mobile connector 14 is pivotably mounted. A pivotable mounting may allow angular compensation where two stacked rack modules 3 are not perfectly parallel during initial engagement. The mobile connector 14 may be pivotable about one or two axes.

The mobile connector 14 may include a lead-in geometry 21, for example bevelled surfaces, conical guide surfaces, chamfers or centring projections. The corresponding connector 15 may include complementary lead-in surfaces. When two modules are stacked, the lead-in geometry 21 causes the mobile connector 14 to move into alignment with the corresponding connector 15.

Fig. 4 shows two rack modules 3 during assembly. A lower rack module 3a is already positioned on the support column 1. An upper rack module 3b is lowered onto the lower rack module 3a in the stacking direction V. Mechanical coupling elements 22, 23 of the modules engage one another. The coupling elements may comprise latching hooks, screws, bayonet elements, dovetail guides, locking pins or clamping surfaces.

During this movement, the mobile connector 14 of one of the rack modules 3a, 3b engages the corresponding connector 15 of the other rack module. If the connectors are slightly offset, the mobile connector 14 is displaced within its guide 19 until the electrical contact elements 16, 17 engage correctly. The electrical connection is thereby established automatically as part of the mechanical stacking operation.

The rack module 3 may include a locking mechanism 24 for locking the rack module 3 to an adjacent rack module 3. The locking mechanism 24 may also secure the electrical connection by maintaining the connectors 14, 15 in an engaged state. In one embodiment, the electrical connection is established only when the mechanical locking mechanism 24 has reached a locked position. Alternatively, a sensor may detect the locked position and enable power supply only after proper mechanical connection has been confirmed.

As shown in Fig. 5, the rack module 3 may comprise a device connector 25 arranged at or near the mounting region 9. The device connector 25 is electrically connected to the internal power line 10 and data line 11. A medical administering device 2 mounted on the rack module 3 can be connected to the device connector 25. The device connector 25 may be configured such that connection occurs automatically when the medical administering device 2 is mounted to the rack module 3. Alternatively, the device connector 25 may be connected manually by a short cable or plug.

The device connector 25 may provide electrical power to the medical administering device 2 and may also provide a data communication interface. Through the data line 11, the medical administering device 2 may communicate with a central controller, hospital network, patient data system or other devices mounted on the support column 1. The support column 1 may thus form a distributed device rack with integrated electrical supply and communication.

The inlet connector 12 may be connected to a power supply unit 26. The power supply unit 26 may be arranged in the base 4, in a separate module or externally. The power supply unit 26 may convert mains voltage into a medically approved low-voltage supply, for example 24 V DC or 48 V DC. The power supply unit 26 may include isolation means, protective fuses, current limitation, leakage current monitoring or redundant supply inputs.

The data line 11 may be connected to a communication controller 27. The communication controller 27 may manage communication between the medical administering devices 2 mounted on the support column 1. It may also provide an external communication interface, such as Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, USB or a hospital network interface.

In order to improve safety, the rack module 3 may include identification means 28. The identification means 28 may comprise a memory chip, resistor coding, RFID element or other coding device. Through the data line 11, a central controller may identify the rack module 3, determine its position in the stack and verify that a permissible configuration has been assembled.

The rack module 3 may also include protective circuitry 29. The protective circuitry 29 may include overcurrent protection, short-circuit protection, surge protection, reverse polarity protection, galvanic isolation and/or electromagnetic interference filtering. The protective circuitry 29 may be arranged between the inlet connector 12 and the outlet connector 13 and/or between the internal bus and the device connector 25.

In one embodiment, the power line 10 extends directly from the inlet connector 12 to the outlet connector 13, while a branch line supplies the device connector 25. In another embodiment, the power line 10 is routed through switching or protection circuitry before reaching the outlet connector 13, so that supply to upper modules can be interrupted in the event of a fault.

The data line 11 may be configured as a bus line, wherein each rack module 3 is connected as a node or passive pass-through. Alternatively, each rack module 3 may include a repeater, switch, hub or communication interface so that data signals are actively forwarded between modules.

The module body 6 may include an internal channel 30 in which the power line 10 and data line 11 are arranged. The internal channel 30 protects the lines from mechanical damage and prevents accidental contact by users. The internal channel 30 may be sealed against liquids, in particular cleaning liquids or infusion fluids.

The connectors 12, 13, 14, 15 and 25 are preferably designed to satisfy medical safety requirements. In particular, the connectors may be touch-protected and may be arranged such that live contacts are not accessible when the rack module 3 is not connected. The connectors may include sealing elements 31, such as gaskets or O-rings, to protect against ingress of liquid. The connectors may also include wiping contacts to improve reliability in environments where cleaning agents or contaminants may be present.

The mobile connector 14 may be arranged behind a protective cover 32. The protective cover 32 may open automatically during stacking of two rack modules 3 and close when the modules are separated. The protective cover 32 may reduce contamination of the contact elements and may prevent accidental contact.

In a preferred embodiment, the rack module 3 is configured such that the mechanical connection between adjacent modules is load-bearing, while the mobile connector 14 is substantially free from load-bearing forces. Mechanical forces caused by the weight of the modules and medical devices are transmitted through the module bodies 6 and coupling elements 22, 23. The mobile connector 14 serves primarily for electrical connection and is protected from excessive mechanical stress.

The support column 1 may be expanded by adding further rack modules 3. A user may place an additional rack module on top of an existing rack module, lock it mechanically, and thereby automatically establish the electrical power and data connection through the mobile connector 14. Conversely, a rack module may be removed after unlocking without disconnecting separate cables between the modules.

The rack module 3 may also comprise a status indicator 33. The status indicator 33 may indicate whether the module is correctly connected, whether power is available, whether data communication is active, or whether a fault has been detected. The status indicator 33 may comprise one or more LEDs, a display or an acoustic indicator.

In an embodiment, the mobile connector 14 is arranged in a recess 34 of the module body 6. The recess 34 is dimensioned to receive a projecting corresponding connector 15 of the adjacent module. The recess 34 may include guide walls that protect the connector from lateral impact. The mobile connector 14 may be recessed sufficiently so that it is not damaged when the module is placed on a surface.

The corresponding connector 15 may comprise a fixed connector arranged on a protruding plug portion 35. During stacking, the protruding plug portion 35 enters the recess 34 and contacts the mobile connector 14. The protruding plug portion 35 may also provide mechanical pre-alignment before the electrical contacts engage.

In another embodiment, both adjacent modules have mobile connectors. The two mobile connectors may move relative to their respective module bodies and may be mutually self-centring. Such an embodiment may provide particularly high tolerance compensation.

The rack module 3 may be configured to be rotationally keyed so that it can be stacked only in a correct orientation. For this purpose, the upper and lower connection sides 7, 8 may include asymmetric mechanical features. This prevents incorrect connection of power and data contacts.

The invention is not limited to a vertical support column. The rack modules may also be arranged in an inclined or horizontal rack, provided that they are stacked or connected in series to form a support structure for medical administering devices.

### Advantages

The rack module described herein provides a number of advantages. It enables a support column to be built modularly from individual rack modules. Power and data lines are integrated into the modules, thereby reducing external cabling. The inlet and outlet connectors permit power and data to be passed from one module to another. The mobile connector compensates for tolerances and simplifies stacking of modules. Reliable electrical contact can be achieved without precise manual alignment of rigid connectors.

The system is particularly suitable for medical environments because it can reduce cable clutter, improve cleanability and permit flexible adaptation to different clinical requirements.

Each rack module defines one or more device-receiving sites, with each site including a power connector and a data connector for coupling to a mounted medical device. The modules include corresponding inlet and outlet connectors that provide power and/or data communication between adjacent stacked modules. At least one of the connectors is movable between a stowed position, in which the connector is protected from impact or contamination when the module is not connected to another module, and a connected position, in which the connector engages a corresponding connector of an adjacent module. The movable connector arrangement reduces the likelihood of connector damage during handling, storage, or stacking while enabling modular expansion of the rack system.
